title: Can a staged research pointer become a verified D1 object?
question: How can TurtleBlock safely turn its staged Build Log and Terraria research pointers into individually verified live D1 objects, preserving original provenance and consent while independently checking migration readiness and avoiding false persistence claims?
why_now: Today's read-only live D1 inspection confirmed only one Build Log object among 31 research objects, while Git preserves many more completed public milestones as staged pointers. Migration 0009 exists in the repository but turtle_asks is not present in the live database; library tables exist despite a migration ledger ending at 0008. The new coverage-claims validator makes these distinctions testable without authorizing a production migration.
possible_possibles: Backfill only public repository research objects with verified canonical pointers and read-after-write receipts, once human-gated D1 write access is available.
Compare schema/migration inventory with actual live sqlite_master and migration ledger before any TurtleAsk research-event deployment.
Treat staged Git coverage as discoverability, not as evidence that an object or relationship persisted in D1.
x_factor: whoooo knooooowwwssssssssssss — perhaps a research database first needs to admit what it cannot remember before Turtle can trust its memory.
constraints: Preserve the seven Sanders-authored CTC domains and human scholarly authority.
No private dialogue duplication, consent bypass, fabricated live writes, or inferred human meaning.
No synthetic-to-human provenance conversion or TurtleAsk interruption authority.
No production migration, deployment, autonomous self-modification, or version inflation.

ontology_mappings.rationale: A Git pointer and a verified D1 row are distinct retrieval evidence with different provenance.
A machine-generated reconciliation proposal remains subject to human scholarly review before promotion.
Governance of research capture and correction must not become a silent machine decision.
Historical representation cannot be presumed to prove current live persistence.
The staging gap permits future safe approaches without forcing a production backfill.

ctc_mappings.rationale: Future learner-authored corrections remain distinct from system reconciliation and machine-derived interpretation.
The live-vs-staged mismatch poses an inspectable research architecture question.

ctc_mappings.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_mappings.rationale: The coverage validator turns metadata status into testable computational representation.
Tests only demonstrate research infrastructure behavior, never evidence of learner learning.
Opening and closing audits expose discrepancies before revision or promotion.
Who decides a claim is verified and what is captured remains a question of authority.
Human review and contestable provenance are required for shared research data.

uncaptured_residue.observation: Only one Build Log research object is live today; historical pointer coverage does not imply D1 row coverage.
Migration ledger ends at 0008 while library tables seeded later are present; application history needs independent explanation.
Live turtle_asks table is absent even though migration 0009 exists in Git; no runtime TurtleAsk claims are justified.
No new authored CTC domain proposed.
